issues.claim: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/fundamentals/object-oriented/ titled "Object-oriented programming in C#" / "Объектно-ориентированное программирование в C#"
issues.problem: The fetched page title is "Classes, structs, and records - C#", not "Object-oriented programming in C#". The excerpt covers class features, inheritance, interfaces, generics and records. Nothing in it supports the encapsulation or exposed-mutable-collection claim, so the link title is wrong and its support for the claim is not shown.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace this link with one the excerpt supports for encapsulation or exposing collections, or keep it and retitle it to match the page ("Classes, structs, and records" / "Классы, структуры и записи"). Cite it only for what it covers, such as the default private accessibility. The guidelines-for-collections and List<T>.AsReadOnly links already carry the main claims.

issues.claim: The .NET design guidelines also advise against `List<T>` in public APIs and recommend `ReadOnlyCollection<T>` for read-only collections.
issues.problem: The claim is supported by the fetched excerpt. The page itself states it is a reprint of the 2008 edition and may be out of date, so it is worth hedging.
issues.suggestedFix: Phrase it as "the Framework Design Guidelines (2nd edition) advise...", or leave as is.

issues.claim: Robert Martin refines it: a module should be responsible to one group of stakeholders. (RU: "Роберт Мартин уточняет: модуль должен отвечать перед одной группой заинтересованных лиц.")
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt of the cleancoder blog URL is only the blog's post-list sidebar, with no text of the SRP article. The attribution to Martin and the wording about stakeholders are not confirmed by the excerpt. The generator notes also say the wording is from memory. The Microsoft Learn page supports only "one responsibility / one reason to change".
issues.suggestedFix: Confirm the wording against the article text. Martin's 2014 post says a module should be responsible to one, and only one, user or stakeholder. Match the answer to that wording, for example "to one user or stakeholder (later: one actor)". If it cannot be confirmed, drop the Martin attribution and the second link.

issues.claim: Подумайте, кто и по каким причинам может попросить изменить каждую из трёх частей этого класса.
issues.problem: The hint almost states the answer hinge (different reasons and stakeholders for change). It is borderline in strength, though it does not name the principle's formulation.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften it, for example: "Представьте, что в проект приходят три разные заявки на изменение: что в классе придётся править?" Apply the same change to the en hint.
